# Two popup-return paths in the workstation leave the pane in its popup

## Context

Operator screen recording, 2026-10-19 13:42Z, the v13.3 cut day: in `apps/workstation`, the v13.2 flagship, a pane torn out by its tab and carried back over the main window does not reintegrate (seconds 15–17). Main paints an accepted tab-into preview under the hand, the release commits the tear-out instead, and the live session's receipt reads `lastCrossWindowTransfer: {applied: true, errors: ['Popup Workspace workstation-vessel:alerts left its pane in provisional chrome']}`. Operator: an issue in the flagship app is a release blocker.

Reproducing it surfaced a second defect on the native title-bar path. Both reproduce in a real browser (Playwright, CDP window moves, the real mouse) on `dev` `ddcd2eddf9` and on the v13.2.0 release source (`b3c78f5523`). Reversing the post-release dock commits (`#19841`, `#19775`, `#19778`) one at a time changes neither: both shipped with v13.2.0.

## The Problem

1. **Edge release (the recording).** Tear a pane out past the window edge, carry the vessel back over main's right column short of the 60 % reattach overlap, and main paints an accepted in-window preview under the pointer. On release the zone is still detached, so it fires `dockTearOutTerminal`: the detach commits and the pane stays in its popup, booted or still booting.
2. **Second title-bar return.** Pop a pane out and return it by its OS title bar; pop a second one out and return it the same way: the second never docks. The first return's vessel stays in `VesselPark.parked`, so every later park is refused (seven retries, then the drop is abandoned without a trace).

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs`: `onDragMove` fires `dockCrossZoneDragMove`, the in-window preview, on every frame, detached or not; `processDragEnd` routes every detached release to `dockTearOutTerminal`.
- Design authority (1): ADR 0029 §2.8.6, amended `#19533`: "inside a window it is that window's tab-header proxy, outside every window it is a vessel, the rule re-entry into the source window always followed."
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPark.mjs`: `onConversionIn` refuses while any slot is held; the coordinator's committed terminal disposes the park. `VesselWorkspace#onNativeWindowRelease` (`apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`) closes the returned vessel once main adopts and clears the coordinator's candidate first, so that terminal never runs, and nothing tells the park.
- Design authority (2): the `VesselPark` contract: "Commit is the ONLY disposition … the slot clears only after strict success", and `onVesselRetired` "Forgets a vessel another owning lifecycle has already retired."
- Coverage: the workstation NL battery returns one popup per session, and its morph arm cancels rather than drops. Hosted CI runs it (`e2e-brain`, blocking, since 2026-10-13) and passed with both bugs in, because no arm made either gesture.

## The Fix

1. `TabSortZone.processDragEnd`: a detached release whose pointer lies inside the source window's drag boundary is a re-entry. The zone fires `dragBoundaryEntry` (the host retires the vessel, zero mutation), then `dockCrossZoneDrop` at the release point. A release outside still fires `dockTearOutTerminal`.
2. `VesselWorkspace#onNativeWindowRelease`: the release retires the park when the released window is the parked vessel's, matched by workspace key or window id.
3. Found while proving (1): the re-entry retires a booted vessel, which leaves the Group while the drop's write prepares, and `Commit` refuses any write whose member set changed. `DragAffordances#onDrop` commits its operation rather than only the document, and `WorkspaceSet#commit` reduces an operation once more at the queue head when that refusal (now `code: 'participants-changed'`) is the reason.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dockTearOutTerminal` (TabSortZone → host) | ADR 0029 §2.8.6 | fires only for a detached release outside the source window | a release inside re-enters and fires `dockCrossZoneDrop` | `processDragEnd` JSDoc | `DockTabSortZone.spec.mjs` arms |
| `VesselPark` slot of a released vessel | `VesselPark` contract | retired by the native release | — | `retireReleasedPark` JSDoc | `Workspace.spec.mjs` arms |
| `Commit` membership refusal | `Commit.run` | the error carries `code: 'participants-changed'` | message unchanged | inline | `DockWorkspaceSetTransaction.spec.mjs` arms |
| dock operation commit (`WorkspaceSet#commit`) | the Group queue head | an operation refused by a membership change is reduced once more | a whole-document write is never re-sent | `commit` JSDoc | `DockWorkspaceSetTransaction.spec.mjs` arms |

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.8.6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A vessel carried back over main and released inside it lands where main previewed it, booted and still booting (real-browser arm).
- [ ] A second popped-out pane docks back by its OS title bar after the first one did (real-browser arm).
- [ ] A detached release outside the window still detaches, and a walk-back while the vessel boots still retires it.
- [ ] Unit arms cover both terminals and the park retirement; dock, workstation and draggable unit directories and the workstation e2e battery stay green.
- [ ] [post-merge] The operator's recorded gesture reintegrates on the merged build.

## Out of Scope

- A native drop that lands while main is still settling a previous return is abandoned on its first null preview instead of awaiting `answerWhenPreviewable` (follow-up).

once, and retries only while the host still resolves the Group the first
attempt went to; otherwise the original refusal surfaces."

* fix(dock): a popup carried back over main lands where main previewed it, and a second titlebar return docks (#19866)

A tear-out released inside its source window, short of the reattach overlap,
still fired dockTearOutTerminal although main painted an accepted preview under
the pointer, so the pane detached into its popup. TabSortZone now treats a
detached release inside the window's drag boundary as a re-entry and drops at
the release point (ADR 0029 §2.8.6).

That re-entry retires a booted vessel, which leaves the Group while the drop's
write prepares, and the Group refused the drop. The in-window drop now commits
its operation, and WorkspaceSet.commit reduces an operation refused by a
membership change once more at the queue head; Commit tags that refusal with
code 'participants-changed'.

A popup returned by its OS title bar left its vessel in VesselPark.parked when
main's adoption closed it: the release cleared the coordinator's candidate
before its committed terminal disposed the park, so every later titlebar drop
was refused. The native release now retires the park.
